points.description: The answer conveys that the learning rate sets the speed of convergence towards the minimum: a small rate gives slow, steady progress, and a larger rate speeds it up. Equivalent wording such as 'step size controls how fast the descent moves' earns the mark.

The answer conveys the danger: if the learning rate is too large (above a critical value), the descent becomes unstable and fails to converge (it overshoots and diverges). Mentioning that a high rate causes zigzagging or oscillation without instability is not enough on its own for this mark.

rubric.notes: Two marks, one for each part of the question: the role of the learning rate (controls convergence speed) and the danger (instability when the rate is too high). Full marks need both ideas in plain words; the overdamped/underdamped detail is secondary and does not earn separate marks. A response describing only the role, or only a vague 'too big is bad' with no mention of instability or failure to converge, earns at most one mark.
